speaker: io
say: Those are the captain’s lamps. We should bring them back.
words_shown: Those are the captain’s lamps. We should bring them back.
tone: Practical and warm, already moving. She means every one of them.

speaker: io
say: We’ll bring them home. Every one.
words_shown: We’ll bring them home. Every one.
tone: A steady promise, quiet conviction. “Every one” firm.

speaker: io
say: [softly] I wrote, Nettie. I just never sent them.
words_shown: I wrote, Nettie. I just never sent them.
tone: Quiet and honest, a little ashamed. Not an excuse.

speaker: io
say: Heartsease. She always said I hadn’t any.
words_shown: Heartsease. She always said I hadn’t any.
tone: Half a laugh, half a catch in the throat.

speaker: io
say: [softly] Her boots are still by the door.
words_shown: Her boots are still by the door.
tone: Almost a whisper. She did not expect it to hurt. Keep it small.

speaker: io
say: I know, Kore. I want to.
words_shown: I know, Kore. I want to.
tone: Soft, but decided.

speaker: io
say: Even here they lean north. The way she went.
words_shown: Even here they lean north. The way she went.
tone: Almost to herself, at the window. A slow thought, not alarm.

speaker: io
say: If a wisp comes close, let me hold it first. Just once.
words_shown: If a wisp comes close, let me hold it first. Just once.
tone: Earnest, pleading a little.

speaker: io
say: Every window dark. Kore, there are children here.
words_shown: Every window dark. Kore, there are children here.
tone: Anxious. The healer’s worry.

speaker: io
say: Since when do you ask me to stay behind, Kore?
words_shown: Since when do you ask me to stay behind, Kore?
tone: Surprised, a little amused, searching her face.

speaker: io
say: Look, Kore. Every lamp in Bogmire, going home.
words_shown: Look, Kore. Every lamp in Bogmire, going home.
tone: Relief, counting them in. A little out of breath, the fight just over.

speaker: io
say: Then we go on.
words_shown: Then we go on.
tone: Simple resolve, gentle.

speaker: io
say: There’s the cottage. And the gate lamp, still lit.
words_shown: There’s the cottage. And the gate lamp, still lit.
tone: Looking down from the ship. Soft, a lump in her throat.

speaker: io
say: [softly] Goodbye, Nettie.
words_shown: Goodbye, Nettie.
tone: Barely above a breath, said down toward the town.

speaker: kore
say: [laughs] Twelve lamps leaving all at once. Someone’s putting on a better show than ours.
words_shown: Twelve lamps leaving all at once. Someone’s putting on a better show than ours.
tone: Delighted, a performer admiring a rival act. The laugh comes first and is real. Under it, a flicker she covers.

speaker: kore
say: Or follow them, Io, and see who’s calling them.
words_shown: Or follow them, Io, and see who’s calling them.
tone: Light and teasing, a challenge offered fondly. A little lean on “calling”.

speaker: kore
say: You don’t have to go in, Io.
words_shown: You don’t have to go in, Io.
tone: Gentle, offering a way out. No teasing at all.

speaker: kore
say: You can’t hold them all, Io. You’ll try. I know you’ll try.
words_shown: You can’t hold them all, Io. You’ll try. I know you’ll try.
tone: Fond and rueful. No scolding.

speaker: kore
say: Funny. I can always see how a road ends. Not this one.
words_shown: Funny. I can always see how a road ends. Not this one.
tone: Light on top, puzzled underneath. The last words quieter.

speaker: kore
say: And they’re asleep. Look. The dark isn’t hurting anyone.
words_shown: And they’re asleep. Look. The dark isn’t hurting anyone.
tone: Gentle and reassuring. A true thing, said simply.

speaker: kore
say: [chuckles] That’s me. Sorry about the mugwort.
words_shown: That’s me. Sorry about the mugwort.
tone: Cheerful and not one bit sorry.

speaker: kore
say: Stay behind me, Io. Humour me.
words_shown: Stay behind me, Io. Humour me.
tone: Light words, serious under them. Not a joke.

speaker: kore
say: [quietly] Since tonight.
words_shown: Since tonight.
tone: Very quiet. No laugh. Let it land.

speaker: kore
say: [softly] Never mind the lamps, Io. Watch the moth.
words_shown: Never mind the lamps, Io. Watch the moth.
tone: Soft and rapt, the only still moment she has. Not a rebuke. An invitation.

speaker: kore
say: Then this isn’t the ending. Usually I’d know.
words_shown: Then this isn’t the ending. Usually I’d know.
tone: Thoughtful and unsettled, honest about it.

speaker: kore
say: Say goodbye this time, Io. It helps.
words_shown: Say goodbye this time, Io. It helps.
tone: Gentle and knowing, a friend’s nudge.

speaker: europa
say: [curious] Oh. There’s a thread on each one, pulled tight. Somebody’s sewing.
words_shown: Oh. There’s a thread on each one, pulled tight. Somebody’s sewing.
tone: Delighted at first. The last word slows: she has seen something odd, and is pleased and uneasy at once.

speaker: europa
say: Both. We’ll do both. It’s quicker.
words_shown: Both. We’ll do both. It’s quicker.
tone: Bright and brisk, settling the argument with a grin.

speaker: europa
say: And if they won’t come, captain, I’ll sew them to your hooks.
words_shown: And if they won’t come, captain, I’ll sew them to your hooks.
tone: Playful and sure of herself, a grin in it.

speaker: europa
say: Someone mended this curtain, a long time ago. Badly. I like them.
words_shown: Someone mended this curtain, a long time ago. Badly. I like them.
tone: Inside now. Fond and playful, lightening the room on purpose.

speaker: europa
say: Their threads run right through the wood. Like a seam.
words_shown: Their threads run right through the wood. Like a seam.
tone: Fascinated, a craftswoman’s eye.

speaker: europa
say: The threads all run out across the water. Tight as a drum.
words_shown: The threads all run out across the water. Tight as a drum.
tone: Serious for once, uneasy.

speaker: europa
say: I’d cut it loose if I could. I can’t find where it starts.
words_shown: I’d cut it loose if I could. I can’t find where it starts.
tone: Frustrated, her fingers itching for her shears.

speaker: europa
say: It’s flying west. Toward the moon. Against every thread.
words_shown: It’s flying west. Toward the moon. Against every thread.
tone: Hushed wonder.

speaker: europa
say: [playfully] All twelve, sewn down in blue. Lean all you like, little ones. You’re staying.
words_shown: All twelve, sewn down in blue. Lean all you like, little ones. You’re staying.
tone: Light and quick, teasing the flames as if they were kittens. Pleased with her work.

speaker: europa
say: From up here the Faire looks like a pincushion. Every pin leaning.
words_shown: From up here the Faire looks like a pincushion. Every pin leaning.
tone: Playful, peering over the rail.

speaker: callisto
say: Every flame in the camp is leaning north-east.
words_shown: Every flame in the camp is leaning north-east.
tone: Quiet and exact. The first to see it. Not alarmed, just sure.

speaker: callisto
say: The lamp by the gate is lit. Someone’s kept it.
words_shown: The lamp by the gate is lit. Someone’s kept it.
tone: Quiet noticing. The first to see it.

speaker: callisto
say: [quietly] Something’s moving in the thorns. Wisps. Going our way.
words_shown: Something’s moving in the thorns. Wisps. Going our way.
tone: Low and alert, a hunter keeping her voice down.

speaker: callisto
say: No lamps at all. And they’re managing.
words_shown: No lamps at all. And they’re managing.
tone: Calm and approving, a little moved.

speaker: callisto
say: Where I grew up, the dark lasted my whole life. You learn the way by hand.
words_shown: Where I grew up, the dark lasted my whole life. You learn the way by hand.
tone: Quiet and unhurried. The most she has ever said about herself.

speaker: callisto
say: Did it hurt anyone?
words_shown: Did it hurt anyone?
tone: Quiet and direct. The question that matters.

speaker: callisto
say: There. In the reeds. It’s full of lamps.
words_shown: There. In the reeds. It’s full of lamps.
tone: Low and certain, pointing.

speaker: callisto
say: It’s seen us.
words_shown: It’s seen us.
tone: Flat and calm. A warning.

speaker: callisto
say: The flames still lean.
words_shown: The flames still lean.
tone: Quiet and plain. The one who always sees it.

speaker: callisto
say: Look back once. Then don’t.
words_shown: Look back once. Then don’t.
tone: Calm advice from someone who has done it.

speaker: odile
say: Don’t look at me. Look at my flames.
words_shown: Don’t look at me. Look at my flames.
tone: Calm, dry, a little stern. She means it kindly, and she is not joking.

speaker: odile
say: Two fingers’ width, every flame on my stall. And not a breath of wind.
words_shown: Two fingers’ width, every flame on my stall. And not a breath of wind.
tone: Precise, measuring with her eyes as she says it. The last words quiet and puzzled.

speaker: odile
say: Go to the captain. He’s at the jetty, past the town, on the lake.
words_shown: Go to the captain. He’s at the jetty, past the town, on the lake.
tone: Brisk and clear, a good guide. A small worry for him under it.

speaker: odile
say: The cold lights? Flames that leaned too far, I’d guess, and never stood back up.
words_shown: The cold lights? Flames that leaned too far, I’d guess, and never stood back up.
tone: Thoughtful, half to herself. A trade secret, offered as a guess.

speaker: odile
say: Three fingers now. I never had cause to measure a flame before tonight.
words_shown: Three fingers now. I never had cause to measure a flame before tonight.
tone: Quiet, a little shaken, covering it with exactness.

speaker: odile
say: The captain’s lamps come home blue at the root. Wherever they went was cold.
words_shown: The captain’s lamps come home blue at the root. Wherever they went was cold.
tone: Reading the flame like a page. Thoughtful, a slight chill on “cold”.

speaker: odile
say: Every land buys my lamps for the dark. I never stay to see them lit.
words_shown: Every land buys my lamps for the dark. I never stay to see them lit.
tone: Matter-of-fact on top, wistful underneath. Do not sweeten it.

speaker: odile
say: Four fingers now. The town says its chimney smoke leans too.
words_shown: Four fingers now. The town says its chimney smoke leans too.
tone: A dry report, with worry held level.

speaker: odile
say: I’ve put the shutters up. I won’t sell a lamp I can’t promise will stay.
words_shown: I’ve put the shutters up. I won’t sell a lamp I can’t promise will stay.
tone: Plain and proud, a little ashamed of the shutters. The last word firm.

speaker: odile
say: [softly] The lamps behind my shutters are still lit. I couldn’t put them out. Not tonight.
words_shown: The lamps behind my shutters are still lit. I couldn’t put them out. Not tonight.
tone: Soft, almost a confession. “Not tonight” very quiet.

speaker: odile
say: They lean a finger less than at dusk. The shutters can come down.
words_shown: They lean a finger less than at dusk. The shutters can come down.
tone: Dry, quietly pleased. She will not make more of it than that.

speaker: odile
say: Lamps for sale. They’ll stay lit. I won’t promise which way they point.
words_shown: Lamps for sale. They’ll stay lit. I won’t promise which way they point.
tone: Back to trade, dry and wry, a twinkle in the last sentence.

speaker: odile
say: They still lean. A flame that leans that long wants something badly.
words_shown: They still lean. A flame that leans that long wants something badly.
tone: Low and thoughtful, looking north-east. The last two words weighed.

speaker: odile
say: The gate keeper counted the lamps. I measured them. Between us, we know nothing.
words_shown: The gate keeper counted the lamps. I measured them. Between us, we know nothing.
tone: Dry and self-mocking, fond of the gate keeper.

speaker: odile
say: The dyer says my flames are paler. I don’t see colour. I see lean.
words_shown: The dyer says my flames are paler. I don’t see colour. I see lean.
tone: Mildly put out. A craftswoman’s pride.

speaker: odile
say: You’ve met the captain. He never says please. He always means it.
words_shown: You’ve met the captain. He never says please. He always means it.
tone: Fond and amused, a long friendship in it.

speaker: odile
say: So Io grew up here. That’s why she looks south, and not at my flames.
words_shown: So Io grew up here. That’s why she looks south, and not at my flames.
tone: Gentle and noticing, a small smile.

speaker: odile
say: You four came in bright. A fight does that. Like a wick just trimmed.
words_shown: You four came in bright. A fight does that. Like a wick just trimmed.
tone: Approving, sizing them up, warm.

speaker: odile
say: You’ve come back guttering, all four. Sit by my lamps a while.
words_shown: You’ve come back guttering, all four. Sit by my lamps a while.
tone: Concerned and kind, firm about the sitting.

speaker: odile
say: You four flicker like a flame in a draught. It settles, with use.
words_shown: You four flicker like a flame in a draught. It settles, with use.
tone: Kindly teaching, not unkind about it.

speaker: odile
say: You burn steady now, you four. I’d sell you as a set.
words_shown: You burn steady now, you four. I’d sell you as a set.
tone: A dry compliment, the joke underplayed.

speaker: odile
say: Don’t brush my glass going by.
words_shown: Don’t brush my glass going by.
tone: Called after them, sharp but not cross. A habit.

speaker: odile
say: All twelve home. I’ve not been so glad of a flame since I was a girl.
words_shown: All twelve home. I’ve not been so glad of a flame since I was a girl.
tone: Moved, and trying not to be. Warm.

speaker: odile
say: None of the captain’s lamps home yet. The sky over the lake looks bare.
words_shown: None of the captain’s lamps home yet. The sky over the lake looks bare.
tone: Quiet worry, looking off toward the lake.

speaker: tully
say: I count everything through this gate. Tonight, something went out that never came in.
words_shown: I count everything through this gate. Tonight, something went out that never came in.
tone: Flat, careful, slow. Unsettled, and hiding it. The last three words matter most.

speaker: tully
say: Every cold light leaves by the same road. At my gate, that means the show’s over.
words_shown: Every cold light leaves by the same road. At my gate, that means the show’s over.
tone: Dry and certain, someone who has watched a thousand crowds go home. Held as a guess, not news.

speaker: tully
say: The lamps were the captain’s. He’s at the jetty, past the town, on the lake.
words_shown: The lamps were the captain’s. He’s at the jetty, past the town, on the lake.
tone: Brisk directions, a little put out about the lamps. Clear on the place.

speaker: tully
say: I’ve kept the gate open past closing. For you four. Don’t tell the watchman.
words_shown: I’ve kept the gate open past closing. For you four. Don’t tell the watchman.
tone: Gruff and a little embarrassed. The warmth is in the small stop before “for you four”.

speaker: tully
say: Out and back, every time. I’ve stopped counting you four. Nearly.
words_shown: Out and back, every time. I’ve stopped counting you four. Nearly.
tone: The thaw. Dry, almost fond. A small stop before “nearly”, which is a joke.

speaker: tully
say: Four out. Bring back four.
words_shown: Four out. Bring back four.
tone: Called after them as they pass the gate. Short and plain. Not quite a blessing.

speaker: bashir
say: You’ll be wanting blue. There is none. Europa bought every skein.
words_shown: You’ll be wanting blue. There is none. Europa bought every skein.
tone: Slow, sideways, deadpan. A pause after “none”.

speaker: bashir
say: Any colour left out long enough goes grey. Those lights have faded, I think.
words_shown: Any colour left out long enough goes grey. Those lights have faded, I think.
tone: Unhurried, a craftsman’s certainty, held lightly as a guess.

speaker: bashir
say: Ask the lamp-seller, by the well. She reads flames the way I read cloth.
words_shown: Ask the lamp-seller, by the well. She reads flames the way I read cloth.
tone: Plain respect for a fellow trade. Short and helpful.

speaker: bashir
say: My reds run to one side of the pot tonight. I’ve stopped stirring.
words_shown: My reds run to one side of the pot tonight. I’ve stopped stirring.
tone: Quiet unease, said as if about the weather.

speaker: bashir
say: Bogmire’s lit, they say. I’ll dye something yellow. I never dye yellow.
words_shown: Bogmire’s lit, they say. I’ll dye something yellow. I never dye yellow.
tone: Dry. A rare small joy he will not show.

speaker: bashir
say: Mind your sleeves. Blue doesn’t come out.
words_shown: Mind your sleeves. Blue doesn’t come out.
tone: Murmured as they pass, not looking up from the pot.

speaker: zofia
say: Sit. No coin tonight. I don’t want paying for what the cards are saying.
words_shown: Sit. No coin tonight. I don’t want paying for what the cards are saying.
tone: The grand manner dropped for once. Low, unsettled, honest.

speaker: zofia
say: Callisto’s card. A woman with a bow, watching a door nobody else has noticed.
words_shown: Callisto’s card. A woman with a bow, watching a door nobody else has noticed.
tone: Laying the card down slowly, reading it as she speaks.

speaker: zofia
say: Europa’s card. Shears over a thread. It can’t decide if it’s mending or cutting.
words_shown: Europa’s card. Shears over a thread. It can’t decide if it’s mending or cutting.
tone: Puzzled, a little amused.

speaker: zofia
say: Io’s card. A letter, sealed and never sent. Don’t look at me like that.
words_shown: Io’s card. A letter, sealed and never sent. Don’t look at me like that.
tone: Gentle on the card, then quick and defensive on the last sentence.

speaker: zofia
say: [quietly] Kore’s card is the blank one. Every deck has one. I’ve never turned it up before.
words_shown: Kore’s card is the blank one. Every deck has one. I’ve never turned it up before.
tone: Hushed, really shaken. The last sentence almost a whisper.

speaker: zofia
say: The cards keep showing a woman with green hands. Try the herb stall in the town square.
words_shown: The cards keep showing a woman with green hands. Try the herb stall in the town square.
tone: Brisk professional advice, a touch of the theatre back in her voice.

speaker: zofia
say: The cards have calmed. Not quiet. Calmer. I’ll take calmer.
words_shown: The cards have calmed. Not quiet. Calmer. I’ll take calmer.
tone: Relieved, precise, wry.

speaker: zofia
say: Come back and tell me I was wrong.
words_shown: Come back and tell me I was wrong.
tone: Called after them, half a joke and half a hope.

speaker: linnet
say: Oh, it’s you. I was halfway through a song about you. Don’t listen to the middle.
words_shown: Oh, it’s you. I was halfway through a song about you. Don’t listen to the middle.
tone: Flustered and delighted, the words tumbling out.

speaker: linnet
say: In the old songs, a marsh light is someone who never got home. I hope songs lie.
words_shown: In the old songs, a marsh light is someone who never got home. I hope songs lie.
tone: Softer, almost sung. The last sentence small.

speaker: linnet
say: The captain’s at the jetty, on the lake past the town. Go gently. He’s sulking.
words_shown: The captain’s at the jetty, on the lake past the town. Go gently. He’s sulking.
tone: Helpful, then lowering her voice for the last bit, as a secret.

speaker: linnet
say: My oldest song has no last verse. Tonight I nearly know it.
words_shown: My oldest song has no last verse. Tonight I nearly know it.
tone: Wondering, a little haunted, quiet.

speaker: linnet
say: I’ll put tonight in a song. I’ll make you four taller.
words_shown: I’ll put tonight in a song. I’ll make you four taller.
tone: Bubbling and teasing, happy.

speaker: linnet
say: Come back for the last verse.
words_shown: Come back for the last verse.
tone: Called after them, warm and hopeful.

speaker: otto
say: You four look like you’ve seen something. Eat first. Then tell me.
words_shown: You four look like you’ve seen something. Eat first. Then tell me.
tone: Big, warm, insistent. Already holding out bread.

speaker: otto
say: Bread taken out too soon goes hard. I think those lights left too soon.
words_shown: Bread taken out too soon goes hard. I think those lights left too soon.
tone: Thoughtful for once. A baker’s sorrow.

speaker: otto
say: Odile at the lamp stall knows flames. I know crusts. She’s by the well.
words_shown: Odile at the lamp stall knows flames. I know crusts. She’s by the well.
tone: Cheerful and self-mocking, pointing the way.

speaker: otto
say: Every loaf’s come out leaning. The town will eat crooked bread and like it.
words_shown: Every loaf’s come out leaning. The town will eat crooked bread and like it.
tone: Indignant and funny, fists on hips.

speaker: otto
say: I’ve baked for the road. Wherever you four fly, you’re not flying hungry.
words_shown: I’ve baked for the road. Wherever you four fly, you’re not flying hungry.
tone: Proud and fond, a little gruff to hide it.

speaker: otto
say: Let it come. I’ve got my peel.
words_shown: Let it come. I’ve got my peel.
tone: Shouted at the dark as they pass, waving his bread peel. Comic bravado.

speaker: corwin
say: I did the lamps before the shutters tonight. First time in forty years.
words_shown: I did the lamps before the shutters tonight. First time in forty years.
tone: Gruff and unsettled, as if owning up to a lapse.

speaker: corwin
say: I’ve led sleepwalkers back to bed. Those lights walk the same. Eyes open, nobody home.
words_shown: I’ve led sleepwalkers back to bed. Those lights walk the same. Eyes open, nobody home.
tone: Slow and steady, an old man’s certainty, kind. Held as a guess.

speaker: corwin
say: Three rounds tonight, every lamp leaning the same. I’ve stopped blaming the wind.
words_shown: Three rounds tonight, every lamp leaning the same. I’ve stopped blaming the wind.
tone: Tired and plain, a little grim humour.

speaker: corwin
say: Lamps still lean, but folk are sleeping. That’s a watch I’ll take.
words_shown: Lamps still lean, but folk are sleeping. That’s a watch I’ll take.
tone: Content, gruffly gentle.

speaker: corwin
say: Your captain’s pacing the jetty, past the town, on the lake. He wants to fly.
words_shown: Your captain’s pacing the jetty, past the town, on the lake. He wants to fly.
tone: Matter-of-fact, a smile in “wants to fly”.

speaker: corwin
say: Back before my last round, you four.
words_shown: Back before my last round, you four.
tone: A gruff order that is really a blessing.

speaker: ros
say: Have you four eaten? Don’t lie. I can see your ribs from here.
words_shown: Have you four eaten? Don’t lie. I can see your ribs from here.
tone: Loud and mothering, mock stern.

speaker: ros
say: Nobody walks that fast unless they owe somebody. Those lights owe somebody, mark me.
words_shown: Nobody walks that fast unless they owe somebody. Those lights owe somebody, mark me.
tone: A trader’s knowing guess, a wink in it.

speaker: ros
say: See the captain at the jetty, by the lake. And see he’s eaten.
words_shown: See the captain at the jetty, by the lake. And see he’s eaten.
tone: Brisk orders, fond under the bossiness.

speaker: ros
say: Frightened folk eat. I’m not proud of it, but I’m not giving it back.
words_shown: Frightened folk eat. I’m not proud of it, but I’m not giving it back.
tone: Brassy honesty, laughing at herself.

speaker: ros
say: Every pie gone. Best night in years. I hated it.
words_shown: Every pie gone. Best night in years. I hated it.
tone: Tired, rueful, warm.

speaker: ros
say: Hot pies! Pay me later!
words_shown: Hot pies! Pay me later!
tone: A cheerful market shout.

speaker: kofi
say: Chestnuts, free. In return, you tell me something nobody else knows.
words_shown: Chestnuts, free. In return, you tell me something nobody else knows.
tone: Bright and bargaining, eyes twinkling.

speaker: kofi
say: Those lights are news, if you ask me. News runs to whoever wants it most.
words_shown: Those lights are news, if you ask me. News runs to whoever wants it most.
tone: Leaning in to confide, pleased with his idea.

speaker: kofi
say: A herb woman from town came asking after Io. Her stall’s in the town square.
words_shown: A herb woman from town came asking after Io. Her stall’s in the town square.
tone: Gossip delivered with relish.

speaker: kofi
say: Half the camp’s at my brazier tonight. Not for chestnuts. For a fire that stays.
words_shown: Half the camp’s at my brazier tonight. Not for chestnuts. For a fire that stays.
tone: Gentler than usual, understanding.

speaker: kofi
say: Bogmire’s lit! I heard it first. Don’t spoil it, let me tell you.
words_shown: Bogmire’s lit! I heard it first. Don’t spoil it, let me tell you.
tone: Bursting with it. Comic urgency.

speaker: kofi
say: Chestnuts for the road!
words_shown: Chestnuts for the road!
tone: Called out cheerfully, waving.

speaker: bridie
say: Don’t stand between me and my lamp. It’s had a bad night.
words_shown: Don’t stand between me and my lamp. It’s had a bad night.
tone: Crotchety and tender, as about a sick child.

speaker: bridie
say: A lamp left burning for someone who never comes back goes strange. Wanders, I’d guess.
words_shown: A lamp left burning for someone who never comes back goes strange. Wanders, I’d guess.
tone: Plain and slow, a little sad.

speaker: bridie
say: The herb woman in the town square keeps that cottage. She’d know.
words_shown: The herb woman in the town square keeps that cottage. She’d know.
tone: Nodding up the road. Plain information.

speaker: bridie
say: I lit the lamp at the cottage gate every night it stood empty. Nobody asked me to.
words_shown: I lit the lamp at the cottage gate every night it stood empty. Nobody asked me to.
tone: Stubborn pride, and something softer under it.

speaker: bridie
say: There. It’s standing almost straight. I’ll trim it and leave it be.
words_shown: There. It’s standing almost straight. I’ll trim it and leave it be.
tone: Gentle satisfaction, half to the lamp.

speaker: bridie
say: Go careful. It’s dark past my lamp.
words_shown: Go careful. It’s dark past my lamp.
tone: Called after them, a grandmother’s warning.

speaker: jory
say: Hello! Sorry. Hello. Did you see them? The lamps? They went right over me!
words_shown: Hello! Sorry. Hello. Did you see them? The lamps? They went right over me!
tone: Fast and breathless, frightened and excited at once.

speaker: jory
say: Ponies bolt like that when they hear their herd. Maybe those lights hear theirs.
words_shown: Ponies bolt like that when they hear their herd. Maybe those lights hear theirs.
tone: Working it out aloud, quick and earnest.

speaker: jory
say: The captain’s at the jetty. He shouted at the sky. I didn’t like to stop him.
words_shown: The captain’s at the jetty. He shouted at the sky. I didn’t like to stop him.
tone: Rushed, half laughing, pointing.

speaker: jory
say: I’ve cut enough rushes for every pony twice. I’m not walking home past those lights.
words_shown: I’ve cut enough rushes for every pony twice. I’m not walking home past those lights.
tone: Trying to sound casual, and failing.

speaker: jory
say: I walked home past where the lights were. Nothing. I’m telling everyone I was brave.
words_shown: I walked home past where the lights were. Nothing. I’m telling everyone I was brave.
tone: Proud and sheepish, grinning.

speaker: jory
say: Good luck! I mean it! Good luck!
words_shown: Good luck! I mean it! Good luck!
tone: Shouted after them, eager.

speaker: captain
say: You’ll be the Faire’s four. Good. I’ve lost my whole crew.
words_shown: You’ll be the Faire’s four. Good. I’ve lost my whole crew.
tone: Flat and clipped, deadpan. Let “crew” land and hang there.

speaker: captain
say: Twelve lamps, torn from their hooks. Bring them home. I don’t lift dark.
words_shown: Twelve lamps, torn from their hooks. Bring them home. I don’t lift dark.
tone: Short and firm, no pleading. The last three words are a rule he has kept all his life.

speaker: captain
say: Twelve bare hooks. I keep looking up at them.
words_shown: Twelve bare hooks. I keep looking up at them.
tone: Flat. A man not admitting he is upset.

speaker: captain
say: That’s another home. I’ll hang it myself. Nobody touches my lamps.
words_shown: That’s another home. I’ll hang it myself. Nobody touches my lamps.
tone: Gruff relief, possessive, tender underneath.

speaker: captain
say: Every lamp you bring, she sits higher at her mooring. Breathing easier.
words_shown: Every lamp you bring, she sits higher at her mooring. Breathing easier.
tone: Softer, almost private. He is talking about his ship.

speaker: captain
say: Anything not tied down drifts. Those cold lights weren’t tied down, I’d say.
words_shown: Anything not tied down drifts. Those cold lights weren’t tied down, I’d say.
tone: A sailor’s plain sense, held as a guess.

speaker: captain
say: [quietly] I flew dark once. Young, and sure of myself. Once.
words_shown: I flew dark once. Young, and sure of myself. Once.
tone: Very quiet, no self-pity. A long breath before the last word, which is the whole story.

speaker: captain
say: Don’t ask me about it. I’ll only tell you, and then I’ll have told you.
words_shown: Don’t ask me about it. I’ll only tell you, and then I’ll have told you.
tone: Dry, turning it aside with half a smile. Back to his usual voice.

speaker: captain
say: My pennant’s standing out straight with no wind under it. Pointing north-east.
words_shown: My pennant’s standing out straight with no wind under it. Pointing north-east.
tone: A weather eye, uneasy, matter-of-fact.

speaker: captain
say: From the deck I can see every window in town. Every flame leaning.
words_shown: From the deck I can see every window in town. Every flame leaning.
tone: Low and troubled, looking out.

speaker: captain
say: Bogmire, then. Dark all the way, they say. Take a lamp. Not mine.
words_shown: Bogmire, then. Dark all the way, they say. Take a lamp. Not mine.
tone: Gruff. The last sentence a dry joke.

speaker: captain
say: If you find any of mine in that fen, they’ll be the cross ones.
words_shown: If you find any of mine in that fen, they’ll be the cross ones.
tone: Deadpan, fond of his lamps.

speaker: captain
say: Any sailor with sense would fly the other way. Get aboard.
words_shown: Any sailor with sense would fly the other way. Get aboard.
tone: Gruff and decided. A smile he will not let anyone see.

speaker: captain
say: Up you come. Sit anywhere that isn’t the wheel.
words_shown: Up you come. Sit anywhere that isn’t the wheel.
tone: Brisk, almost cheerful. A host on his own deck.

speaker: captain
say: Some of my lamps are still out. Bring them and we fly.
words_shown: Some of my lamps are still out. Bring them and we fly.
tone: Impatient and hopeful, businesslike.

speaker: captain
say: Bogmire’s lit and mine still lean. Whatever’s pulling, it’s further than the fen.
words_shown: Bogmire’s lit and mine still lean. Whatever’s pulling, it’s further than the fen.
tone: Thoughtful, looking north-east. A sailor reading a long weather.

speaker: captain
say: All twelve home, and leaning on their hooks. I’ll not lift like that.
words_shown: All twelve home, and leaning on their hooks. I’ll not lift like that.
tone: Stubborn and careful. No argument.

speaker: captain
say: The ones you’ve brought tug at their hooks, like dogs that smell something.
words_shown: The ones you’ve brought tug at their hooks, like dogs that smell something.
tone: Uneasy, half to himself.

speaker: captain
say: Twenty years I’ve flown for the Faire. Never once lost a lamp. Until tonight.
words_shown: Twenty years I’ve flown for the Faire. Never once lost a lamp. Until tonight.
tone: Proud, and then the last two words drop.

speaker: captain
say: Mind the planks. They’re older than me.
words_shown: Mind the planks. They’re older than me.
tone: Called after them, dry.

speaker: captain
say: The pie-seller’s been at you about me. I’m fed. Tell her I’m fed.
words_shown: The pie-seller’s been at you about me. I’m fed. Tell her I’m fed.
tone: Exasperated and fond, a man mothered against his will.

speaker: captain
say: The lamp-seller sold me those lamps when I was green. She’ll want to know they’re home.
words_shown: The lamp-seller sold me those lamps when I was green. She’ll want to know they’re home.
tone: A warm memory, respectful.

speaker: captain
say: The gate keeper counted my lamps over. Twelve. As if I didn’t know.
words_shown: The gate keeper counted my lamps over. Twelve. As if I didn’t know.
tone: Dry irritation, secretly amused.

speaker: captain
say: Quill’s been telling you stories. Half of them are mine. The good half.
words_shown: Quill’s been telling you stories. Half of them are mine. The good half.
tone: Deadpan, a hint of pride.

speaker: captain
say: You came back with that look. A crew that’s ridden out a squall.
words_shown: You came back with that look. A crew that’s ridden out a squall.
tone: Approving, a captain’s nod.

speaker: captain
say: Took a beating. Sit on the crates a while. Nobody’s flying yet.
words_shown: Took a beating. Sit on the crates a while. Nobody’s flying yet.
tone: Gruff kindness, no fuss.

speaker: captain
say: You four stand like landsmen on a rolling deck. That’ll pass.
words_shown: You four stand like landsmen on a rolling deck. That’ll pass.
tone: Wry, not unkind.

speaker: captain
say: You’ve found your sea legs, all four. I’d sail with you.
words_shown: You’ve found your sea legs, all four. I’d sail with you.
tone: Plain respect, the highest he gives.

speaker: quill
say: Rope, line, or a knot while you wait. Tonight I’d tie down anything that burns.
words_shown: Rope, line, or a knot while you wait. Tonight I’d tie down anything that burns.
tone: Easy patter, then the last sentence serious.

speaker: quill
say: Sailors call them lost lanterns. Hunting a harbour that isn’t there any more.
words_shown: Sailors call them lost lanterns. Hunting a harbour that isn’t there any more.
tone: Old sailors’ lore, told low.

speaker: quill
say: For the town? See Nettie in the square. She knows everybody’s business.
words_shown: For the town? See Nettie in the square. She knows everybody’s business.
tone: Friendly, a chuckle on the last part.

speaker: quill
say: I’ve tied my lantern to its post with three hitches. It’s still trying.
words_shown: I’ve tied my lantern to its post with three hitches. It’s still trying.
tone: Wry, a little rattled.

speaker: quill
say: The captain’s whistling on his deck. Sailors only whistle when they’re leaving.
words_shown: The captain’s whistling on his deck. Sailors only whistle when they’re leaving.
tone: Knowing, gently sad.

speaker: quill
say: Fair winds, you four.
words_shown: Fair winds, you four.
tone: A sailor’s farewell, warm.

speaker: nettie
say: Io. Seven summers I’ve watered your garden, and not one letter.
words_shown: Io. Seven summers I’ve watered your garden, and not one letter.
tone: A fond scold that does not hold. Glad to see her, and cross about being glad.

speaker: nettie
say: Go and see the cottage, Io. Up the hill, past the camp. It’s waited long enough.
words_shown: Go and see the cottage, Io. Up the hill, past the camp. It’s waited long enough.
tone: Brisk, to cover the feeling. Gentle on the last sentence.

speaker: nettie
say: The garden’s yours. I only watered it. The rosemary did the rest.
words_shown: The garden’s yours. I only watered it. The rosemary did the rest.
tone: Modest and fond, waving it off.

speaker: nettie
say: My drying herbs hang crooked tonight, every bunch. I’ve retied them twice.
words_shown: My drying herbs hang crooked tonight, every bunch. I’ve retied them twice.
tone: Fussed and puzzled, a practical woman annoyed.

speaker: nettie
say: Those cold lights are like seedlings in a dark shed. Pale, leaning at the crack.
words_shown: Those cold lights are like seedlings in a dark shed. Pale, leaning at the crack.
tone: Thoughtful, a gardener’s eye. Held as a guess.

speaker: nettie
say: You’ve been up to the cottage. I can smell the lavender on you.
words_shown: You’ve been up to the cottage. I can smell the lavender on you.
tone: Pleased and knowing, a sniff and a smile.

speaker: nettie
say: Did you go in, Io? I never did. Not once in seven years.
words_shown: Did you go in, Io? I never did. Not once in seven years.
tone: Careful and gentle, a little proud of keeping out.

speaker: nettie
say: The morning your sister went north, Io, she bought heartsease off me. [gently] She said it was for you.
words_shown: The morning your sister went north, Io, she bought heartsease off me. She said it was for you.
tone: Gentle and careful, telling something she has kept a long time. Slower at the end.

speaker: nettie
say: She said she’d be home before the frost. That was eight frosts ago.
words_shown: She said she’d be home before the frost. That was eight frosts ago.
tone: Plain and quiet, no tears in it, which is worse.

speaker: nettie
say: If anyone’s still in Bogmire, it’s Old Wenna. Past the Thornwood, out in the fen.
words_shown: If anyone’s still in Bogmire, it’s Old Wenna. Past the Thornwood, out in the fen.
tone: Practical, a little worried. Directions given like a recipe.

speaker: nettie
say: For the fen? Take my sage. It won’t help, but it’ll smell like home.
words_shown: For the fen? Take my sage. It won’t help, but it’ll smell like home.
tone: Brisk mothering, a sad joke at the end.

speaker: nettie
say: Tell Old Wenna the marigolds came up. She’ll want to know.
words_shown: Tell Old Wenna the marigolds came up. She’ll want to know.
tone: Light. A small errand to keep the worry busy.

speaker: nettie
say: Word’s come up from Bogmire. Every window lit. I cried into my thyme.
words_shown: Word’s come up from Bogmire. Every window lit. I cried into my thyme.
tone: Laughing at herself through tears.

speaker: nettie
say: Go on with the Faire, Io. I’ll keep the garden. Gardens wait better than people.
words_shown: Go on with the Faire, Io. I’ll keep the garden. Gardens wait better than people.
tone: Warm, letting her go. A small smile on the last line, so it does not break.

speaker: nettie
say: I’ll write to you, Io. And you’ll not answer, and I’ll write again.
words_shown: I’ll write to you, Io. And you’ll not answer, and I’ll write again.
tone: Fond teasing, with the ache under it.

speaker: nettie
say: So the chestnut man told you I’d been asking. I had. Twice.
words_shown: So the chestnut man told you I’d been asking. I had. Twice.
tone: Caught out, and owning it with a laugh.

speaker: nettie
say: The mayor will tell you the town’s fine. The town’s not fine. The town’s leaning.
words_shown: The mayor will tell you the town’s fine. The town’s not fine. The town’s leaning.
tone: Tart and plain, a neighbour’s exasperation.

speaker: nettie
say: Hilde’s banked her forge to the roof. She thinks fire answers everything.
words_shown: Hilde’s banked her forge to the roof. She thinks fire answers everything.
tone: An affectionate grumble.

speaker: nettie
say: You’ve a cut, Io. Hold still. I don’t care that you’re the healer.
words_shown: You’ve a cut, Io. Hold still. I don’t care that you’re the healer.
tone: Bossy and loving. No argument allowed.

speaker: nettie
say: Sit down, all of you. Feverfew, and a cup of something. Don’t argue.
words_shown: Sit down, all of you. Feverfew, and a cup of something. Don’t argue.
tone: Quick and firm, already fetching things.

speaker: nettie
say: You four look picked too early. You’ll ripen.
words_shown: You four look picked too early. You’ll ripen.
tone: Kindly, a gardener’s judgement.

speaker: nettie
say: Look at you four. Like a good hedge. Nothing gets through that.
words_shown: Look at you four. Like a good hedge. Nothing gets through that.
tone: Proud and admiring.

speaker: nettie
say: Off you go, and back you come.
words_shown: Off you go, and back you come.
tone: Called after them, warm, in a mother’s rhythm.

speaker: nettie
say: Your lamps go home over the square. The children count them.
words_shown: Your lamps go home over the square. The children count them.
tone: Delighted, watching the sky.

speaker: gretch
say: I’m the mayor, for my sins. I’ll say it plain. Every flame in Wickhollow leans.
words_shown: I’m the mayor, for my sins. I’ll say it plain. Every flame in Wickhollow leans.
tone: Blunt and tired, a man who has said it ten times tonight.

speaker: gretch
say: A hundred lamps in this town, all pointing the same way. Folk are frightened.
words_shown: A hundred lamps in this town, all pointing the same way. Folk are frightened.
tone: Plain worry, no drama.

speaker: gretch
say: Folk leave a town when they’ve heard of somewhere better. Those lights have heard something.
words_shown: Folk leave a town when they’ve heard of somewhere better. Those lights have heard something.
tone: A mayor’s weary wisdom. A guess.

speaker: gretch
say: Nobody’s come up the Thornwood road from Bogmire in weeks. Ask Old Wenna there.
words_shown: Nobody’s come up the Thornwood road from Bogmire in weeks. Ask Old Wenna there.
tone: Worried and direct.

speaker: gretch
say: The town wants me to do something. I’ve lit more lamps. They lean too.
words_shown: The town wants me to do something. I’ve lit more lamps. They lean too.
tone: Helpless humour, a shrug in the voice.

speaker: gretch
say: Io’s home, they tell me. Good. The town’s missed that family.
words_shown: Io’s home, they tell me. Good. The town’s missed that family.
tone: Gruff warmth, sincere.

speaker: gretch
say: Bogmire’s lit. I’ll say it plain. Thank you. There. I’ve said it.
words_shown: Bogmire’s lit. I’ll say it plain. Thank you. There. I’ve said it.
tone: Awkward gratitude, embarrassed and sincere.

speaker: gretch
say: Keep to the road, you four.
words_shown: Keep to the road, you four.
tone: Called after them, a mayor’s caution.

speaker: hilde
say: My forge has never disobeyed me. Tonight it’s leaning out of the door.
words_shown: My forge has never disobeyed me. Tonight it’s leaning out of the door.
tone: Offended pride, more indignant than afraid.

speaker: hilde
say: A fire draws hardest when a door’s open somewhere. Something’s left one open.
words_shown: A fire draws hardest when a door’s open somewhere. Something’s left one open.
tone: A smith’s practical sense, a little ominous.

speaker: hilde
say: Nettie’s kept your cottage, Io. Across the square, at the herb stall.
words_shown: Nettie’s kept your cottage, Io. Across the square, at the herb stall.
tone: Kind and plain, nodding the way.

speaker: hilde
say: I’ve banked her as high as she’ll go. She only leans higher.
words_shown: I’ve banked her as high as she’ll go. She only leans higher.
tone: Frustrated, speaking of the forge like a stubborn horse.

speaker: hilde
say: I let the forge die down tonight, and she stayed put.
words_shown: I let the forge die down tonight, and she stayed put.
tone: Relieved, a quiet pride.

speaker: hilde
say: Mind the sparks.
words_shown: Mind the sparks.
tone: Called over the hammer.

speaker: wenna
say: Stand still, you four. You’re about to walk into my mugwort.
words_shown: Stand still, you four. You’re about to walk into my mugwort.
tone: Sharp but amused. An old woman who heard them coming.

speaker: wenna
say: Faire folk, by the sound of you. I can hear the bells.
words_shown: Faire folk, by the sound of you. I can hear the bells.
tone: Pleased with her ears, dry.

speaker: wenna
say: Something came out of the fen and took every lamp in Bogmire. Mine off my sill.
words_shown: Something came out of the fen and took every lamp in Bogmire. Mine off my sill.
tone: Plain telling, no fear in it, a little indignant.

speaker: wenna
say: Tall as the inn. Lamps burning in its ribs like a cage of birds.
words_shown: Tall as the inn. Lamps burning in its ribs like a cage of birds.
tone: Slower, remembering. Let the picture land.

speaker: wenna
say: Not a soul. It looked lost, more than cruel.
words_shown: Not a soul. It looked lost, more than cruel.
tone: Gentle and thoughtful. Pity turns in her voice.

speaker: wenna
say: It sits in the fen’s dark heart. Up the north road, where the boardwalk ends.
words_shown: It sits in the fen’s dark heart. Up the north road, where the boardwalk ends.
tone: Clear directions, pointing into the dark.

speaker: wenna
say: They’re cold when they pass. Not unkind cold. The cold of a house nobody lives in.
words_shown: They’re cold when they pass. Not unkind cold. The cold of a house nobody lives in.
tone: Slow and careful, finding the words. A guess.

speaker: wenna
say: I sell by touch now. Nobody’s been cheated yet. Nobody can see to check.
words_shown: I sell by touch now. Nobody’s been cheated yet. Nobody can see to check.
tone: Dry humour, a twinkle.

speaker: wenna
say: The children stopped being frightened. It’s the grown ones who sit up all night.
words_shown: The children stopped being frightened. It’s the grown ones who sit up all night.
tone: Wry, and tender about the town.

speaker: wenna
say: You can live in the dark, you know. It’s only the cold that’s hard.
words_shown: You can live in the dark, you know. It’s only the cold that’s hard.
tone: A simple truth, matter-of-fact.

speaker: wenna
say: Go kindly, if you go to it. It never took a life. Only lamps.
words_shown: Go kindly, if you go to it. It never took a life. Only lamps.
tone: Earnest. A plea.

speaker: wenna
say: Lamps in every window, and I can read my labels. My writing’s dreadful.
words_shown: Lamps in every window, and I can read my labels. My writing’s dreadful.
tone: Delighted, laughing at herself.

speaker: wenna
say: I’ll tell you a thing. I’d got used to the dark. It was honest.
words_shown: I’ll tell you a thing. I’d got used to the dark. It was honest.
tone: Confiding and slow, a little wistful.

speaker: wenna
say: The lamps still lean, mind. Like they’ve remembered something.
words_shown: The lamps still lean, mind. Like they’ve remembered something.
tone: Low and uneasy, thinking.

speaker: wenna
say: Pell’s told you it wasn’t frightening. Pell’s right. Don’t tell Pell I said so.
words_shown: Pell’s told you it wasn’t frightening. Pell’s right. Don’t tell Pell I said so.
tone: Gruffly fond, conspiratorial.

speaker: wenna
say: So Nettie sent you. Did she mention the marigolds? She’ll have mentioned the marigolds.
words_shown: So Nettie sent you. Did she mention the marigolds? She’ll have mentioned the marigolds.
tone: Amused exasperation. An old friendship.

speaker: wenna
say: I can hear you breathing hard. Won, then. Losers breathe quieter.
words_shown: I can hear you breathing hard. Won, then. Losers breathe quieter.
tone: Dry and sharp-eared, approving.

speaker: wenna
say: I heard you go down in the reeds. Sit. I’ll find something by feel.
words_shown: I heard you go down in the reeds. Sit. I’ll find something by feel.
tone: Practical kindness, already reaching for a jar.

speaker: wenna
say: Mind the boards. The third one’s soft.
words_shown: Mind the boards. The third one’s soft.
tone: Called after them. A local’s warning.

speaker: wenna
say: Something’s going over, high. One of your lamps? It sounds glad.
words_shown: Something’s going over, high. One of your lamps? It sounds glad.
tone: Listening upward, wonder in it.

speaker: tobb
say: Come in. Don’t mind the dark. It’s the cheapest thing in the house.
words_shown: Come in. Don’t mind the dark. It’s the cheapest thing in the house.
tone: A big, gentle welcome. A joke he has made before.

speaker: tobb
say: Folk too tired to stop walk straight past an inn. Those lights walk past mine.
words_shown: Folk too tired to stop walk straight past an inn. Those lights walk past mine.
tone: An innkeeper’s observation, slow and sad. A guess.

speaker: tobb
say: Old Wenna saw it take the lamps. Her herb stall’s by the boardwalk.
words_shown: Old Wenna saw it take the lamps. Her herb stall’s by the boardwalk.
tone: Helpful, voice lowered.

speaker: tobb
say: I set a candle in the window every night. Unlit. It’s manners.
words_shown: I set a candle in the window every night. Unlit. It’s manners.
tone: Plain and quietly dignified.

speaker: tobb
say: Every room lit, and nobody can sleep for the brightness. Give them a week.
words_shown: Every room lit, and nobody can sleep for the brightness. Give them a week.
tone: A wry, happy grumble.

speaker: tobb
say: Bed’s here when you want it.
words_shown: Bed’s here when you want it.
tone: Called after them, warm.

speaker: pell
say: I’m not scared. Everyone else is scared. I’m not.
words_shown: I’m not scared. Everyone else is scared. I’m not.
tone: Firm and proud, a child’s certainty.

speaker: pell
say: They’re only lost. You don’t be scared of lost things. You help them.
words_shown: They’re only lost. You don’t be scared of lost things. You help them.
tone: Patient, explaining the obvious to grown-ups.

speaker: pell
say: Old Wenna saw where it went. She’s on the boardwalk. She gives sweets.
words_shown: Old Wenna saw where it went. She’s on the boardwalk. She gives sweets.
tone: Helpful, and conspiratorial about the sweets.

speaker: pell
say: I waved at it once. It didn’t wave back. I think it forgot how.
words_shown: I waved at it once. It didn’t wave back. I think it forgot how.
tone: Thoughtful and kind, not sad.

speaker: pell
say: The lights came home over the water. I lost count. It was good.
words_shown: The lights came home over the water. I lost count. It was good.
tone: Delighted and breathless.

speaker: pell
say: I’m still not scared!
words_shown: I’m still not scared!
tone: Shouted after them, proud.
